title: SampledCompositeSmoothConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F(x)=Eξ[loss(ξ,x)]+ψ(x) over a nonempty closed convex set Q. Every sampled loss is convex, and ψ is convex on Q and lower semicontinuous. A minimizer x⋆ exists.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: The expected smooth loss is combined with a potentially nonsmooth convex regularizer and a constraint set; exact proximal minimization includes both ψ and Q.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query at x returns grad(ξ,x), the exact gradient of a fresh IID sampled loss. The law and sampled functions are hidden instance data. No function values or reusable sample identifiers are returned.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: For a>0, a query (a,z,g) returns an exact minimizer over Q of ‖u−z‖²/(2a)+⟨g,u−z⟩+ψ(u). Gradient and proximal queries each consume one call from the same oracle budget.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Only solution variance is bounded: Eξ‖grad(ξ,x⋆)−Eζ grad(ζ,x⋆)‖²≤σ² at a minimizer satisfying the initialization bounds. There is no uniform variance bound over x, bounded-gradient assumption, or exponential-tail assumption.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, possibly infinite-dimensional. Every sampled gradient is globally L-Lipschitz. Public parameters include x0,L,R,Δ,σ,ε, with L,R,ε>0 and Δ,σ≥0; x0∈Q, ‖x0−x⋆‖≤R, and F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ. Q need not be bounded.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned E-valued point must be measurable, its objective gap integrable, and E[F(output)−F(x⋆)]≤ε for a minimizer over Q. The successful predicate does not separately require output∈Q or specify averaging; allowedAlgorithm restricts the permitted algorithm family.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee is in expectation over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, under a fixed total oracle budget; it is not a high-probability guarantee.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: An established stochastic composite convex optimization formulation with IID sample gradients, samplewise smoothness, solution-only variance control, exact proximal access, and expected objective error. The Hilbert-space scope and restricted algorithm family require separate applicability checks.

descriptionHtml:
Proximal Linear-Decay SGD

We consider minimizing F(x)=Eξ∼ν[ℓ(ξ,x)]+ψ(x) over a closed convex set Q in a separable real Hilbert space E, where ν is a probability law on a measurable sample space Ξ. Each sample loss ℓ(ξ,⋅) is convex with an L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0, and ψ:E→R is lower semicontinuous and convex on Q. A given starting point has bounded distance and objective gap to a minimizer x⋆, where gradient variance is bounded. The oracle returns independent sampled gradients or exact proximal minimizers. Proximal SGD with linearly decaying steps must return a measurable output x¯ with integrable gap satisfying E[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where ε>0 and expectation is over the samples.

Write f(x)=Eξ∼ν[ℓ(ξ,x)],F(x)=f(x)+ψ(x). The optimization problem is minx∈QF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, Ξ, the starting point x0, and the parameters L>0,R>0,Δ≥0,σ≥0,ε>0. The model consists of ν, ℓ, its sample gradient g:Ξ×E→E, ψ, Q, and a proximal map P:R×E×E→E; access to it is through the oracle below.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Sample losses). The map (ξ,x)↦g(ξ,x) is jointly measurable. For every ξ∈Ξ, the function ℓ(ξ,⋅) is convex and Fréchet differentiable on E, with g(ξ,x)=∇xℓ(ξ,x),∥g(ξ,x)−g(ξ,y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E. For every x∈E, the function ξ↦ℓ(ξ,x) is integrable under ν.

Assumption 2 (Composite structure and proximal access). The set Q⊆E is closed and convex, and x0∈Q. The function ψ:E→R is lower semicontinuous on E and convex on Q. For every a>0 and z,h∈E, the oracle’s proximal map satisfies P(a,z,h)∈argminu∈Q{∥u−z∥22a+⟨h,u−z⟩+ψ(u)}. The map is defined for all real a, but this minimization property is required only for a>0.

Assumption 3 (Initialization and variance at a minimizer). There exists x⋆∈Q such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈Q,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,F(x0)−F(x⋆)≤Δ. The random vector g(ξ,x⋆) is Bochner integrable under ν. Define its mean by m⋆=Eξ∼ν[g(ξ,x⋆)]. The squared centered norm is integrable and satisfies Eξ∼ν[∥g(ξ,x⋆)−m⋆∥2]≤σ2.

Let (ξj)j≥0 be measurable, mutually independent samples, each with law ν, and let P denote their joint law. At call j, a gradient query x∈E returns g(ξj,x), while a proximal query (a,z,h)∈R×E×E returns P(a,z,h). Both query types count toward one shared oracle-call budget; proximal replies do not depend on the sample at that call.

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze proximal SGD with linear step-size decay. The algorithm chooses η≥0 and an integer T≥0 from its inputs and starts at the given x0. It alternates a gradient query and a proximal query according to ak=ηT−kT,hk=g(ξ2k,xk),xk+1=P(ak,xk,hk),k=0,1,…. When T=0, the step-size formula is interpreted as ak=0. The parameter T specifies the decay schedule; termination is determined by the allotted number of calls. For a budget of N≥0 calls, the output is the last completed proximal iterate, x¯=x⌊N/2⌋. Thus each completed update uses two calls, and an additional gradient call does not change the output.

The output must be measurable under P, and its objective gap must be integrable and satisfy EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Ahmed Khaled, Othmane Sebbouh, Nicolas Loizou, Robert M. Gower, Peter Richtárik. Complexity: O(1+(LR2+Δ)/ε+σ2R2/ε2) total stochastic-gradient and exact proximal oracle calls, with a fixed budget, for averaged proximal SGD achieving expected composite objective gap at most ε.

comparisonHtml:
Minimize Φ=f+ψ on a closed convex set Q in a second-countable real Hilbert space, with f(x)=∫Fξ(x)dp(ξ). Each integrable sample loss is convex and globally L-smooth; sample gradients are jointly measurable. The real-valued ψ is lower semicontinuous and convex on Q; its constrained prox is exact. IID samples have law p. A minimizer x⋆∈Q satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R, Φ(x0)−Φ(x⋆)≤Δ, and ∫∥∇Fξ(x⋆)−∇f(x⋆)∥2dp(ξ)≤σ2. Here x0∈Q, L,R,ε>0, Δ,σ≥0. The setup restricts the algorithm to proximal SGD with linear decay and last-iterate output xT; the target is ∫[Φ(xT(ω))−Φ(x⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε for the IID trajectory law P.

Log-free proximal-SGD guarantee; deterministic regularization can have σ=0<σ⋆. (1) needs R,σ for steps; Δ for stopping. Requires finite ψ on closed Q, excluding barrier regularizers.
(3) Derived bound: averaged proximal SGD (Garrigos and Gower 2024, Theorem 12.5); finite-dimensional finite sum, components bounded below; tuned constant step O(1+LR2ε+Δε

(4) Linear-decay proximal SGD (Liu and Zhou 2026, Theorems 3.4/C.3); finite-dimensional, uniformly bounded variance O(1+LR2ε+σu2R2ε2) (1) needs variance only at x⋆, covering regularized random-design least squares with σu=∞. Scope extension, not a rate improvement at equal noise. (1) needs samplewise convexity and smoothness; adds Δ/ε; lacks Bregman geometry. Assumption classes are incomparable.
(5) SAGD (Ilandarideva et al. 2024, Corollary 1, (3.6)); ψ=0 on Q, finite-dimensional, unit batches O(1+LR2ε+σ2R2ε2) (1) extends scope to nonzero ψ using proximal SGD. On the overlap, matches order if Δ=O(LR2+σ2R2/ε). (1) is worse when Δ≫LR2+σ2R2/ε.

Abbr: Costs count sample-gradient and exact constrained-prox calls (one each per iteration; projection when ψ=0). σ⋆2=σ2+∥∇f(x⋆)∥2 bounds the gradient second moment at x⋆. σu2 bounds gradient variance uniformly. In (5), the state-dependent variance parameters specialize to L=4L and noise 2σ2. T is the iteration horizon; SGD denotes stochastic gradient descent.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function

namespace OracleTemplate.SampledComposite

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

noncomputable def path {Ξ : Type*} (grad : Ξ → E → E) (prox : ℝ → E → E → E) (η : ℝ) (T : ℕ)
    (x0 : E) (ξ : ℕ → Ξ) : ℕ → E
  | 0 => x0
  | k + 1 =>
    prox (η * ((T : ℝ) - k) / T) (path grad prox η T x0 ξ k)
      (grad (ξ (2 * k)) (path grad prox η T x0 ξ k))

noncomputable def proximalLinearDecaySgd (η : ℝ) (T : ℕ) (x0 : E) :
    Algorithm (E ⊕ (ℝ × E × E)) E E where
  State := ℕ × Bool × E × E
  initial _ := (0, false, x0, 0)
  query s :=
    if s.2.1 then (0, Sum.inr (η * ((T : ℝ) - s.1) / T, s.2.2.1, s.2.2.2))
    else (0, Sum.inl s.2.2.1)
  update s r := if s.2.1 then (s.1 + 1, false, r, s.2.2.2) else (s.1, true, s.2.2.1, r)
  output s := s.2.2.1

end OracleTemplate.SampledComposite

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.SampledCompositeSmoothConvex

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.SampledComposite

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ξ : Type
  [measurableΞ : MeasurableSpace Ξ]
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE Params.borelE
  Params.countableE Params.measurableΞ

structure Model (E Ξ : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ξ] where
  law : ProbabilityMeasure Ξ
  loss : Ξ → E → ℝ
  grad : Ξ → E → E
  ψ : E → ℝ
  Q : Set E
  prox : ℝ → E → E → E

noncomputable def smoothPart {E Ξ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] (M : Model E Ξ) (x : E) : ℝ :=
  ∫ ξ, M.loss ξ x ∂(M.law : Measure Ξ)

noncomputable def objective {E Ξ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] (M : Model E Ξ) (x : E) : ℝ :=
  smoothPart M x + M.ψ x

noncomputable def proxObjective {E Ξ : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [MeasurableSpace Ξ] (M : Model E Ξ) (a : ℝ) (z g u : E) : ℝ :=
  ‖u - z‖ ^ 2 / (2 * a) + ⟪g, u - z⟫ + M.ψ u

noncomputable def oracleAnswer {E Ξ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] (M : Model E Ξ)
    (query : Fin 1 × (E ⊕ (ℝ × E × E))) (ξ : Ξ) : E :=
  match query.2 with
  | Sum.inl x => M.grad ξ x
  | Sum.inr (a, z, g) => M.prox a z g

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Model p.E p.Ξ
  Query p := p.E ⊕ (ℝ × p.E × p.E)
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  allowedAlgorithm q algorithm :=
    ∃ (η : ℝ) (T : ℕ), 0 ≤ η ∧ algorithm = proximalLinearDecaySgd η T q.x0
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q M O :=
    ∃ P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ξ),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ξ) => ξ k)
      (M.law : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ξ
          law := P
          answer := fun _ query ξ => oracleAnswer M query ξ } ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry M.grad) ∧
    (∀ ξ, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (M.loss ξ)) ∧
    (∀ ξ x, HasGradientAt (M.loss ξ) (M.grad ξ x) x) ∧
    (∀ ξ x y, ‖M.grad ξ x - M.grad ξ y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ξ => M.loss ξ x) (M.law : Measure q.Ξ)) ∧
    Convex ℝ M.Q ∧
    IsClosed M.Q ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ M.Q M.ψ ∧
    LowerSemicontinuous M.ψ ∧
    (∀ a, 0 < a → ∀ z g, M.prox a z g ∈ M.Q ∧ IsMinOn (proxObjective M a z g) M.Q (M.prox a z g)) ∧
    q.x0 ∈ M.Q ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ M.Q, IsMinOn (objective M) M.Q xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧
      objective M q.x0 - objective M xstar ≤ q.Δ ∧
      Integrable (fun ξ => M.grad ξ xstar) (M.law : Measure q.Ξ) ∧
      Integrable (fun ξ => ‖M.grad ξ xstar - ∫ ζ, M.grad ζ xstar ∂(M.law : Measure q.Ξ)‖ ^ 2)
        (M.law : Measure q.Ξ) ∧
      ∫ ξ, ‖M.grad ξ xstar - ∫ ζ, M.grad ζ xstar ∂(M.law : Measure q.Ξ)‖ ^ 2 ∂(M.law : Measure q.Ξ) ≤
        q.σ ^ 2)
  successful q M output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    ∃ xstar ∈ M.Q, IsMinOn (objective M) M.Q xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective M (output ω) - objective M xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, objective M (output ω) - objective M xstar ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SampledCompositeSmoothConvex
